title: UK unis must treat compliance as “strategic institutional risk”
summary_en: UK universities must be proactive in managing compliance risks if they want to avoid falling foul of the new BCA thresholds, an immigration expert has warned.
author: Beth Kennedy
title_cn: UK unis must treat compliance as “strategic institutional risk”

title: Brand alone “no longer enough” in Asia’s international school markets, IPSEF told
summary_en: The international schools sector continues to grow rapidly, with more than 14,000 schools worldwide, and Asia accounting for the majority of provision, led by China and India – but speakers at IPSEF 2026 warned that the conditions for success in the region are changing fast.
author: The PIE News team
title_cn: Brand alone “no longer enough” in Asia’s international school markets, IPSEF told

title: Nicholas Brain, Jumeirah College
summary_en: This week, The PIE sat down with Nicholas Brain, deputy executive vice president and principal/CEO of Jumeirah College in Dubai. We spoke about the future of schools and how to build a learning environment where young people thrive.
author: The PIE News team

title: Compliance and access dominate university assessment plans, confirms testing giant
summary_en: Growing scrutiny of international student recruitment is prompting universities to place greater emphasis on trusted and accessible English language assessments.
author: Amy Baker
title_cn: Compliance and access dominate university assessment plans, confirms testing giant

title: Explained: How India’s biggest medical entrance exam descended into crisis
summary_en: An alleged paper leak, an unprecedented nationwide retest and mounting political pressure have thrust NEET, India's medical entrance examination, into the spotlight, laying bare the intense pressure and high stakes behind one of the world's largest medical admissions systems.
author: Abhishek Nair
title_cn: Explained: How India’s biggest medical entrance exam descended into crisis
